text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"Mayo Clinic notes that a supplement or a multivitamin with vitamin D may help improve bone health.","cited_pids":["504dd1c8446c#0"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"Mayo Clinic lists a recommended daily vitamin D intake of 600 IU for adults aged 1 to 70.","cited_pids":["504dd1c8446c#0"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"Mayo Clinic lists a recommended daily vitamin D intake of 800 IU for adults over 70.","cited_pids":["504dd1c8446c#0"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"Vitamin D insufficiency and deficiency are common and are linked to higher all-cause mortality.","cited_pids":["92e80c257b2f#0"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"The VITAL and D-Health trials, conducted mostly in vitamin D-sufficient populations, found no mortality benefit from vitamin D supplementation.","cited_pids":["92e80c257b2f#0"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"Trials on vitamin D and fracture outcomes are inconsistent, with some finding benefit and others finding no effect.","cited_pids":["91044cbd3351#0"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"A meta-analysis of healthy elderly adults reports that the fracture benefit of vitamin D supplementation is still unclear.","cited_pids":["0b67acc0837f#0"]},{"cid":"c8","text":"A Health article states that the appropriate dosing frequency depends on how deficient a person is.","cited_pids":["92caed0a21e3#0"]},{"cid":"c9","text":"Daily versus weekly vitamin D dosing should be guided by blood levels.","cited_pids":["92caed0a21e3#0"]},{"cid":"c10","text":"No passage in the set directly contradicts the findings on vitamin D supplementation.","cited_pids":[]}]}
